clue.text: Where pupils may be nearly all casual

parts.note: school pupils are grouped in a class called a form, so they may be in form

indicators.note: nearly signals the word all loses its final letter

parts.note: the word all, cut short

explanation.surface: A remark that schoolchildren are mostly dressed down.
explanation.walkthrough: IN FORM is where pupils may be, since a British school class is a form; 'nearly' trims ALL to AL. The held text runs 'may be' together as 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a relaxed manner or dress, free of ceremony and stiffness.

clue.text: One abandoning clothes on a tour is too often having nought to lose

indicators.note: nought is the letter O, and often says it goes more than once, every O in the phrase

explanation.surface: A tourist who sheds clothing but keeps losing things.
explanation.walkthrough: Take 'on a tour is too' and delete each O (nought) wherever it appears: four of them go.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist chooses to go without garments.

clue.text: Ask too much concerning Light Brigade's action

parts.note: over can mean about, concerning, as in a row over money
the Charge of the Light Brigade was a cavalry attack in the Crimean War

explanation.surface: A remark about the famous cavalry attack being too demanding.
explanation.walkthrough: The Light Brigade's famous action was its charge at Balaclava in 1854.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand an excessive price is to bill a customer more than is fair.

clue.text: Elevated missile tube opening when going after leaders in Middle Eastern city

indicators.note: going after places the turned pieces behind the leading letters
leaders are the front letters of the two words Middle and Eastern
elevated in a down clue means the pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a silo is the underground shaft from which a missile is launched
a port is an opening, like a porthole or gun port

explanation.surface: A rocket launched from a city in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' reads SILO + PORT upwards as TROPOLIS, which goes after ME, the leading letters of Middle Eastern.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolis is a major city, a capital or great urban centre.

clue.text: Aircraft descent into the French city cleared at last

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: into says the letter goes inside the following pieces

parts.note: a town stands in for city

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of cleared

explanation.surface: A plane coming down into a French city once it is cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: D, the last letter of cleared, goes into LE TOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: When a plane comes down towards the runway, the lowering phase is given this name.

clue.text: When head has book destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed says the book letter is wiped out of the head word

parts.note: bonce is British slang for the head

explanation.surface: Asking when someone's head lost a book.
explanation.walkthrough: BONCE is British slang for the head; 'destroyed' removes B (book).
explanation.definitionFit: As a conjunction it means as soon as, as in 'as soon as you arrive'.

clue.text: Give decoration to historian introducing chapter on king

parts.note: the Venerable Bede wrote an early history of the English church
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A historian adding a chapter about a king to adorn his work.
explanation.walkthrough: Bede introduces C, which sits on K: the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn something is to deck it out with ornaments.

clue.text: A small measure of fear over memory

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: angst is anxiety, dread
ROM is read-only memory in computing

explanation.surface: A slight amount of fear outweighing what we remember.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means above, so ANGST sits on ROM.
explanation.definitionFit: This unit equals one ten-billionth of a metre, used for wavelengths and atoms.

clue.text: Language in Steinbeck shows genius

indicators.note: shows means displays, so the run of letters is on display inside the phrase before it

explanation.surface: Praise for the brilliance of an American novelist's prose.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the last letter of 'Language' and goes through 'in' into 'Steinbeck'; 'shows' signals it. 'Language in Steinbeck' reads as a topic for literary study.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist's surname has become a byword for an outstandingly clever person.

clue.text: Still check if there's time for leading resistance

indicators.note: for marks a swap of one letter for another, and leading says it is the first such letter that goes

parts.note: to check something is to arrest it, halt its progress
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A query about pausing when there is time to lead the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: ARREST has two Rs; 'leading' says the first R (resistance) is replaced by T (time).
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless, not moving at all, is said to be still or in repose.

clue.text: Run like a bull not yielding power to steer

parts.note: R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a run
a bull, being male, has no udder

explanation.surface: Advice to flee from a charging bull that will not give way.
explanation.walkthrough: A bull is male, so it has no udder: UDDERLESS. 'not yielding power to steer' describes a boat that has lost its steering blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel lacking its steering blade cannot be guided, so it gives no control of direction.

clue.text: Mine's hard hats may be made of this

definitions.text: hats may be made of this

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A miner's hard hat and what it is made of.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('has'). The pith helmet, or topi, is a tropical sun hat made from dried plant pith.
explanation.definitionFit: Sun helmets worn in the tropics were traditionally made from the dried spongy tissue of plants.

clue.text: Man right to take in impecunious uncle?

indicators.note: to take in means to enclose, so the first pieces wrap round the next word

parts.note: a pawn is one of the chess men
impecunious means penniless, broke

explanation.surface: A poor relation being given lodging by a decent man.
explanation.walkthrough: PAWN + R takes in BROKE, which goes before the R. 'Uncle' is old slang for the person who lends money on pledged goods, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle is traditional slang for a lender who takes goods as security for cash.

clue.text: Son of Odin died on tree? Rubbish

parts.note: Balder is the Norse god, son of Odin
an ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A Norse god dying on a tree, dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts BALDER and D above ASH in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or senseless talk is called this.

clue.text: Unacceptable, the way Oliver Smith's letters are shown by his lover Tim?

definitions.text: the way Oliver Smith's letters are shown by his lover Tim?

explanation.surface: Outrage at a lover's letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of OLIVER SMITH, rearranged, spell HIS LOVER TIM: they appear jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that breaks the rules is improper; letters set in a jumbled sequence are not in their proper arrangement.

clue.text: Get annoyed after cut stalk is unproductive

indicators.note: after places the annoyance word behind the shortened stalk
a cut stalk is a shortened one, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a stem is the stalk of a plant
rile means to annoy, to get someone's goat

explanation.surface: A gardener vexed that a pruned plant will not bear fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims STEM to STE, and RILE comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A barren plant or animal is one that produces no offspring or fruit.

clue.text: Dearth of motors raising level of sulphur over London?

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second
raising the level of a letter in a down clue moves it higher, to the top

parts.note: motors are cars
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: A shortage of cars pushing sulphur levels up above London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising level of sulphur' moves the S of CARS to the top in this down clue, making SCAR, over CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack of supply, a shortage, is meant by both words.

clue.text: Goods lost as half of family puts in things for auction

indicators.note: puts in means the first piece receives the second inside it
half of takes the front three of the six letters of family

parts.note: lots are the items numbered for sale at an auction

explanation.surface: A family placing items in a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' gives FAM, which 'puts in' LOTS between F and AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating wreckage and cargo from a ship lost at sea are called this.

clue.text: Girl deceived soundly over snake

indicators.note: soundly here says the phrase is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name; conned means tricked, deceived

explanation.surface: A girl thoroughly tricked by a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' but means the girl's name and the verb are spoken: ANNA CONNED. 'over' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This large constrictor of South America is a kind of serpent.

clue.text: Feeling of unease where man embraces ladies regularly

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so the man word wraps the selected letters

parts.note: a male is a man

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth of ladies

explanation.surface: Discomfort where a man hugs ladies on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives AIS from ladies, which MALE embraces.
explanation.definitionFit: A vague sense of discomfort or illness is called this.

clue.text: Soothing spirit, maybe, to take following pudding

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert, the course after the main
to have something is to take it, as in have a drink

explanation.surface: Advice to take a soothing drink after dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts HAVE after AFTERS. The definition's 'spirit' is the alcohol in the lotion applied to the face after a razor.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotion splashed on after a razor is largely alcohol and calms the skin.

clue.text: School leaver Brown, Tom initially seen around Rugby

indicators.note: seen around says the outer pieces enclose the sports abbreviation

parts.note: tan is a brown colour
RU is short for Rugby Union

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of Tom

explanation.surface: Tom Brown, the boy at Rugby School in a Victorian novel, playing hooky.
explanation.walkthrough: TAN + T goes around RU. The surface points to 'Tom Brown's School Days', a novel set at Rugby, an English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil who skips lessons without leave is said to play hooky.

clue.text: Standard variety of plant

explanation.surface: A banner or a plant variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner on a pole; the yellow iris of wet ground is also called by this name.

clue.text: Former PM's measure for harmful burial ground

indicators.note: for marks a swap, the measure standing in place of the harmful word

parts.note: Winston Churchill was a British Prime Minister
ill means harmful, as in ill effects
a yard is a measure of length

explanation.surface: A famous statesman's harmful policy concerning cemeteries.
explanation.walkthrough: In CHURCHILL, the ILL ('harmful') is replaced by YARD ('measure'), reading 'measure for harmful'.
explanation.definitionFit: The enclosed land round a place of worship where the dead are interred.

clue.text: Part of shoe or hard slipper?

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an eel is slippery, so it is a slipper

explanation.surface: A question whether the back of a shoe is a hard slipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipper' is not footwear but a thing that slips: the eel.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised back of a shoe beneath the wearer's foot.

clue.text: Passionate queen in translation of Dante

indicators.note: in says the queen goes inside the rearranged name
a translation renders a text anew, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A fervent queen reading a new translation of Dante's poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation of' turns DANTE into ADENT, and 'in' puts R (Regina) after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is fiery feeling, so an ardent person is eager and fervent.

clue.text: Unpleasant to hear "time" except if holding ale at the end

indicators.note: holding means the conjunction contains the next piece

parts.note: unless means except if

indicators.note: at the end picks the final letter of ale

explanation.surface: A publican's grating call of last orders unless the beer is still being held.
explanation.walkthrough: UNLESS ('except if') holds E, the last letter of ale, and T comes first. The held text has a stray 'a' in 'at the end'.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing or music lacking melody grates on the ear.

clue.text: Spiritual energy follows her and others around

indicators.note: around says the Latin tag goes outside the other pieces

parts.note: et al is short for Latin et alii, and others

indicators.note: follows puts the energy letter after her

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A woman trailed by a spiritual force and other people.
explanation.walkthrough: E follows HER to make HERE, and ET AL ('and others') goes around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unearthly and delicate seems to belong to the heavens rather than the material world.
